caveats: ⚑ skill1 gainPierce is kit-scoped 'for 1 shot' — the engine's gainPierce has only durationSec (no durationShots), so 1.2s is an UNMEASURED stand-in for exactly one full-charge shot (chargeFrames 60 = 1.0s + inter-shot delay). Too long = extra pierce-tagged shots feeding the 13.55% Pierce Damage buff.

⚑ Cadence tuple (pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 141 / chargeFrames 60) is datamined and unreliable, and it drives EVERY threshold in this kit: the 3/5/8-full-charge counters and therefore the team burstCdr rate and the 5.06% uptime. Treat all downstream uptimes as estimates.

⚑ The burst rider block's two branches (parts-hit → coreDamagePct, body-hit → casterAtkPct) are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE per ally per hit in-game; the engine has no per-hitter targeting, so both are authored team-wide. The parts branch is gated requiresCore as a documented proxy (the scope-lock boss has no destructible parts; core is the only non-body area the engine models) — a strict reading would leave the parts branch fully inert. This dual model can OVER-CREDIT when core exposure is high.

⚑ 'allies' normal attack hits …' is an ALLY-hit trigger; engine triggers are owner-scoped, so hitCount:1 on the owner is a stand-in that keeps the 10s riders topped up while Wipe Out is live. It couples the riders' uptime to HER cadence, not the team's.
noFb:true on the 269.28% burst hit follows the burst-cast pre-FB convention (a burst cast lands before the FB window opens), not a measurement.
crit on the 269.28% hit is left unset — flat-damage rider crit eligibility is handled by the engine's global rider-crit path; no core (the text says no core strike).
pierceDamagePct is documented as inert in v1 for the static-tag path; retained verbatim for kit completeness and because this kit self-sources a real pierce tag via skill1.

Methodology note (not a value leak): the types.ts requiresTargetStatus comment discusses a 'Wipe Out' status and a core-only proxy for a parts-hit branch. No slug and no magnitudes for this unit appeared, so I did not declare a leak — but the gate choice above was reachable from the schema comment as well as from the prose.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Blind prose→JSON read of D: Killer Wife (SR/Fire/Supporter/Burst I, ammo 6, chargeFrames 60). Full-kit audit: 8 kit lines, 7 IMPLEMENTED, 1 SKIPPED (the descriptive 'depending on the area hit' umbrella, kept verbatim in unmodeled.burst). Key reads: (1) all three 'attacking with Full Charge for N time(s)' lines are chargeCounter triggers (per-block counters at 3 / 5 / 8), NOT intervals or hit counts; (2) the S1 pierce is a step-gated gainPierce EFFECT, never the whole-fight hasPierce flag — it turns on only after 3 full charges and lasts one shot; (3) the FB-enter Pierce Damage buff is weapon-scoped (alliesOfWeapon SR, self included), not all allies; (4) the burst block is enemy-targeted and carries both the 269.28% instant hit and the 10s wipeOut targetStatus that opens the two rider gates; (5) 'ATK ▲12.19% of the skill user's ATK' is casterAtkPct (flat add resolved at apply time), not atkPct. The burstCdr line is recurring (no oncePerBattle) and is this unit's main support channel — its real value hinges entirely on the ⚑ charge cadence.

flags.reasoning: Kit says 'Gain Pierce for 1 shot' — a SHOT-count window with no engine primitive (gainPierce has durationSec only; durationShots exists only on buff). chargeFrames 60 = 1.0 s charge, so one full-charge shot cycle is ~1.0-1.5 s including the inter-shot/recovery delay. 1.2 s is chosen to cover exactly the next shot without spilling into a second.
flags.recipe: Log shot events for d-killer-wife in a sim run (cfg.onEvent kind 'shot') to get her real full-charge interval; or count full-charge shots per 10 s in footage. Set durationSec just under one interval so exactly ONE shot carries the pierce tag, then verify only one pierce-tagged damage event follows each 3rd charge.

flags.estimate: as datamined (charge 1.0 s, reload 2.35 s, 6 ammo)
flags.reasoning: Datamine cadence fields are known-unreliable, and this kit is unusually cadence-sensitive: EVERY skill1/skill2 trigger is a full-charge counter (3 / 5 / 8), so the charge rate sets the team burstCdr rate, the 5.06% attack-damage uptime, and the pierce-window frequency. A 10% cadence error propagates linearly into all three.
flags.recipe: Count her full-charge shots over a fixed 60 s window of footage (ammo counter 6 → reload cycles are visible) and compare to the sim's shot-event count for the same window; correct chargeFrames/reloadFrames before trusting any uptime number.

flags.reasoning: Convention, not measurement: a burst-cast instant hit resolves before the Full Burst window opens, so it should not take the +50% FB major. Per-kit noFb is otherwise a measured-only field, so this is flagged rather than asserted.
flags.recipe: In footage, compare the 269.28% popup timestamp against the Full Burst banner frame. If the popup lands after the banner, drop noFb (or set burstSnapshotsPreFb appropriately) and re-check the popup magnitude against final ATK × 2.6928 × (1.5 if FB).

flags.field: override.burst[1] (requiresCore parts-hit branch) vs override.burst[2] (body branch)
flags.estimate: both active team-wide; parts branch gated requiresCore
flags.reasoning: In-game the branch is chosen PER ALLY PER HIT (parts vs body) and the two are mutually exclusive; the engine has no per-hitter targeting and the v1 boss has no destructible parts. I model the body branch unconditionally and proxy 'parts' with requiresCore (core is the only non-body area the engine represents). This risks over-crediting when core exposure is high, and a strict partless reading would zero the 16.26% branch entirely.
flags.recipe: On a real fight with a cored boss, read core-hit popups for a teammate during the 10 s Wipe Out window and test whether their core multiplier lifts by 16.26 pts; separately test a body-only ally for the +12.19%-of-caster-ATK flat lift. If both are observed simultaneously on DIFFERENT allies, keep the dual model; if a single ally can only ever hold one, the branch split needs per-hitter targeting (engine gap) and the parts branch should be dropped to unmodeled.

flags.reasoning: Kit-silent trigger from the engine's point of view: the activation clause is 'ALLIES' normal attack hits', but all TriggerDefs are owner-scoped. Keying to her own every-hit keeps the 10 s riders continuously refreshed for as long as Wipe Out (10 s) is live, which matches the intended always-on-during-window shape — but ties rider uptime to HER SR cadence rather than the team's much faster hit stream.
flags.recipe: Confirm the riders are live for the FULL 10 s wipeOut window in a buffApply/expiresFrame trace (stat coreDamagePct / casterAtkPct). If her cadence ever leaves a gap (e.g. across her 141-frame reload), either drop the trigger to a passive with the status gate or extend nothing and record the measured gap — do not lengthen durationSec past the kit's 10 s.
